newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 1.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- A compromise remained elusive as negotiators from the United Automobile Workers union and General Motors Corp held talks in an attempt to settle a labor dispute.
- Jeffrey Vinik, former manager of the Fidelity Magellan fund begins investing an $800 million hedge fund at his new firm, Vinik Asset Management.
- Some analysts worry that the U.S. economy will slip into a recession, while others just see its growth slowing down a bit.
- Conrail Inc is a corporate gem at the heart of the biggest railroad merger battle in the country's history.
- Third-quarter corporate results hint that earnings growth for the next quarter will be the smallest since profits fell in 1991.
- The U.S. National Research Council did not find any convincing evidence that exposure to electric and magnetic fields from power lines and home appliances might be a health hazard.
- Lowe Direct of Lowe & Partners/SMS has filed a lawsuit against a group of former executives who quit and formed their own direct marketing firm.
- Exxon Corp said it had closed the books on its efforts to recover costs from insurance companies in recovering $780 million from a total of $2.5 billion that it paid for the Alaska oil spill.
- Mexican Energy Secretary Reyes Heroles is seeking a compromise on the partial privatization of the state oil company, Petroleos Mexicanos.
- Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Limited Inc filed an anti-trust suit against Visa USA Inc for allegedly obliging them to accept Visa Check cards.
